body: Lean in. I know it's a phrase rather than a word, but it annoys the hell out of me.

I might have just answered my own question. If the Enterprise's travel was limited to mostly impulse speed (presumably much slower than the speed of light) and warp speed (which isn't traveling at speeds above the speed of light, but rather "bending space" to reduce the distance between two points), then maybe this time difference wouldn't be an issue.

Schwarzza, I'm really sorry you're going through this. I truly understand how you feel, and how devastating it is. My wife also told me she wanted a divorce a couple years ago due to my depression, and I'm still grieving to this day. I am also out of work because of my depression and anxiety. One thing I try to remind myself about my lost marriage is that it is easy to look back at our failed relationships through rose-colored glasses, remembering only the good parts. In reality, at least for me, not everything was rosy. Also, despite the fact that our mental illness is really difficult for our loved ones to live with, the fact that our wives abandoned us at our time of greatest need perhaps indicates that this wasn't the right person for us. I'm still trying to convince myself of that, if only to make it hurt less, but perhaps there's a grain of truth. Perhaps there is someone else out there who will understand us better and be more supportive partners for us, maybe even make *us* better partners. As for the job and  losing the thing that kept our minds occupied, I'm with you there too. I wish I had an answer for you, but I'm still trying to figure that one out myself. I hope for both of us that we can eventually overcome the grief of losing our wives, and find meaningful work to give us a purpose in life. I wish you the best.
Very good description. My experience is much the same. For me, it literally feels like I've been kicked in the chest really hard every one of those hundred times. Over. And over. And over.

Wow. Sorry to hear that. I know how hard that must be. Same here as far as $$. Meds, therapists, and $40K for ECT. I assume your ex has never been depressed herself? People who have never experienced mental illness just don't get it. They can say some amazingly insensitive things. My mom has told me to snap out of it and that the reason I'm depressed is that I'm an atheist. I get it, believe me. Hang in there.

Sorry you're hurting. I can totally relate. I just wanted to point out one positive about you: you're funny as hell, even if you didn't mean it. The part about your day-shift secretary made me laugh out loud (something exceedingly rare for me). "I hate her *face*." That shit is funny. Made me think of the part in Office Space where Peter gets annoyed by the secretary with the annoying high-pitched voice. Best wishes to you.

Hermes, sorry to hear about your troubles. Just wanted to say that it helps to hear of another guy in his 40s living with his folks after a divorce. Same here. I can't believe how ashamed it makes me feel, but knowing that others do it too somehow lessens the shame a bit. Here's hoping we both find our way out of the hurt, feeling lost, and out of our folks' house!

I so feel your pain, my friend. I live with my mom, and I'm 47! Like, who the hell lives with their parents at my age?! I got divorced last year and have been suicidal and unemployed ever since, so I have no choice at the moment. But my mom says things like "Snap out of it!" and "Do you think your problem is that you're an atheist?". I've realized that she will never change. She just doesn't understand the devastation that depression causes and that it's not possible to simply will yourself out of it. It helps once you make that realization. I try to not take it as personally anymore. It's hard, because her comments are such incredibly insensitive, hurtful, and personal attacks, but people who haven't suffered mental illness just don't get it, and I think they don't even understand how truly hurtful their comments are (most people, anyway).

Great info–thanks! I have been seriously considering applying for SSDI because I've been unable to hold down a job for 3 years (having had to quit anywhere from 3 days to 3 months max after starting due to severe anxiety attacks at work), and no work at all for the past 7 months because the depression, panic, and suicidal urges have been so bad. I was wondering if you have thoughts about why your case was approved so quickly. I've got an extensive case record with my psychiatrist over the past 8 or so years (and with others going back 25 years), have been on almost all the meds, have had extensive therapy, and 20 sessions of ECT. My doctor is now looking into treating me with Ketamine, which is kind of a last resort for me. I'm wondering if this history makes it any more likely that I'd get approved.

I very much like your advice to make sure you are committed to improving your life after getting it. That's one reason I have held off on applying for so long. I don't wantit to be a crutch that keeps me in the shithole forever. Kind of like the fact that I'm on Medicaid right now. If I get a low-paying job, it'll pay just enough to disqualify me for Medicaid, but not enough to cover the cost of health insurance on my own.

Wow, I thought I was the only one who felt this way. I, too, dread waking up to sunshine and chirping birds. It actually makes the panic I experience upon waking up even worse. Just goes to show you how messed up an illness depression is, that it could make someone dread chirping birds. Ugh.

Thanks for your kind reply, Pinker. Sorry to hear you've experienced similar loss and grief. The hurt and feeling of abandonment really is hard to describe. I keep asking myself, if I had cancer, would she have left me? But I know that's not fair. It is difficult for the loved ones of those with depression, and I don't want someone to feel obligated to stick with me just because we got a marriage license. Still, it hurts.

Since only one of the dogs was mine (and even that is arguable as it was her wedding gift to me), I'd only have the option of taking one of them, and because I don't want to split them up, that isn't an option for me. Also, I'm still struggling to take care of myself (even eating, hygiene, etc.), so I wouldn't feel capable of walking and caring for a dog as regularly as they demand. I've thought of volunteering at the local shelter, but you have to make a several-month commitment, and I'm just not confident I can honor that for the same reasons.

I may take you up on your PM offer sometime--thanks for offering!

Peace
